title: Year two close: the whole Torah
hookLine: the whole Torah, the whole prayer book, the whole year, now known from the inside
carry: the torah, the prayer, the year

lines: THE LAST VERSE OF A BOOK.
cards: Five times a year, something special happens in synagogue. The reader reaches the last verse of one of the Torah's five books.
In some congregations everyone rises, and the whole room calls out three words: chazak, chazak, venitchazek. Be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened. Not well done.
Be strong. This year's lessons reached that shout four times: at the end of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. Today it comes once more, at the end of the whole year.

teach.b: Year two began in the middle of the plagues and walked the people out of Egypt, through the sea, to Sinai, and into a tent of meeting built from everyone's gifts.
Then Leviticus, the book of holiness, with its offerings and its sudden line, in the old Jewish translation: "thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself."

Then Numbers: forty years of wilderness, complaints, manna and a donkey that talked. Then Deuteronomy, Moses' long goodbye, ending on Mount Nebo with a land he could see and not enter, and a grave no one knows.
On Simchat Torah the scroll rolled straight back to the beginning.

teach.h: THE PRAYER BOOK, PAGE BY PAGE.
teach.b: Then the prayer book, in order: thanking God on waking for the rooster's sense to tell day from night; the Shema, a hand over the eyes; the Amidah, feet together, three steps in; Shabbat, and the quiet personal prayers at the end.

Then the year: the Days of Awe, the sukkah, winter's lights, Purim's noise, the Passover table, forty-nine days of counting, Sinai as a wedding, Ruth choosing to stay, and this summer's walls, floor and vineyards.
Three circles, each one turning. The Torah is read through every year and begins again the moment it ends. The prayers come back three times a day.
The year comes back every year.
None is ever finished; that's the point.

teach.h: THE TORAH, THE PRAYER, THE YEAR.
teach.b: So the words at the end of a book don't say you made it. They say be strong, and the plural is the key: let us be strengthened, together.
A people that keeps the same scroll, prayers and days holds each other up by doing it.

how: When the reading of each of the five books of the Torah is completed in the synagogue, the congregation, often standing, calls out "chazak, chazak, venitchazek" (be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened), and the reader repeats it.

o: well done: praise for the reader who finished
be strong: called out at the end of a Torah book
farewell: a goodbye said to the closing book

p: Moses sees the land he won't enter

s: at the end of a book of the Torah the congregation says congratulations
they call out chazak, chazak, venitchazek: be strong, and let us be strengthened.
the Torah's reading begins again as soon as it ends
on Simchat Torah the last verse is followed straight away by the first.
year two finished four books of the Torah

games.q: the reader has just finished the last verse of Deuteronomy. the whole Torah is done. what does the congregation do?
o: close the scroll until next year.
begin again at Genesis straight away.
games.why: on Simchat Torah the first chapter of Genesis is read right after the end of Deuteronomy. the circle never stops.

practice: Let a few of this year's blessings pass by: my God, the soul you placed in me is pure; the one thanking God for strength to the weary; blessed is the one who spoke, and the world came to be.
If you pray, say one slowly, in Hebrew or English; if not, say quietly the one line from this year that stayed with you.

wordCard.voice: Chazak. Be strong: the shout at the end of each book of the Torah, and the word that closes the whole year, each circle beginning again.

orig.note: Hebrew: be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened. said at the end of each book of the Torah.
